evidence: order-mapper.ts: the shared toOrderDto(order: Order) is the only place that maps an Order to a DTO. advance-order-use-case.ts, cancel-order-use-case.ts, list-orders-use-case.ts and place-order-use-case.ts all call it.

advance-order-use-case.ts and list-orders-use-case.ts both check status by calling the domain predicate isOrderStatus. The status rule stays in the domain and is not copied into the application layer.
cancel-order-use-case.ts and place-order-use-case.ts both go through StockAllocationService (release and reserve) and do not change product stock directly.
get-stock-levels-use-case.ts maps Product to StockLevelDto inline. order-mapper.ts has no product mapping, so no existing abstraction is skipped.
order-dto.ts declares StockLevelDto next to the order DTOs. The file name is narrower than its contents, but this is not a split of concerns.
All use-case classes follow the same structure: constructor-injected repositories or services and a single execute() method.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module is one application-service layer for ordering and stock. Every file follows the same pattern: a use-case class takes domain repositories or services through its constructor, exposes a single execute() method and returns DTOs from order-dto.ts.

All four use cases that return an OrderDto (Advance, Cancel, List, Place) build it through the shared toOrderDto in order-mapper.ts. None of them copies the Order-to-DTO mapping.

The order-status check is not duplicated. Advance and List both call the domain predicate isOrderStatus, so the rule itself stays in the domain. Each use case only turns a failed check into its own error message.

The order-not-found guard appears in both AdvanceOrderUseCase and CancelOrderUseCase. It is a small guard clause, not a business rule copied in two places.

Two minor points, neither a violation:
- StockLevelDto lives in order-dto.ts, so the file name is slightly too narrow for what it holds.
- GetStockLevelsUseCase maps products to DTOs inline instead of through a mapper. There is no product mapper in the module, so this does not skip any abstraction the module provides.

The stock use case is closely tied to ordering, since placing and cancelling orders reserve and release stock through StockAllocationService, so the module still covers one concern.
